#375. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

Tanggal: 09 Feb 2022 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/andrew-ng-data-centric-ai

The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big issues.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Berdasarkan laporan, andrew ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. So when he says he has identified the next big shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Diungkapkan bahwa ng’s current efforts are focused on his company landing ai, which built a platform called landinglens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he says can yield “small data” solutions to big issues in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?.

Diungkapkan bahwa andrew ng: this is a big question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?.

Diungkapkan bahwa ng: this is a term coined by percy liang and some of my friends at stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a new paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?.

Berdasarkan laporan, ng: i think there is a scalability problem. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Sebagaimana diketahui, having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of users, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of users.

Berdasarkan laporan, ng: over a decade ago, when i proposed starting the google brain project to use google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “in many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, i think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn. ” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

Diungkapkan bahwa i remember when my students and i published the first neurips workshop paper advocating using cuda, a platform for processing on gpus, for deep learning—a different senior person in ai sat me down and said, “cuda is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work. ” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

Berdasarkan laporan, over the past year as i’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric ai movement, i’ve been getting flashbacks to when i was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing new here” and “this seems like the wrong direction. ”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ng: data-centric ai is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an ai system. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when i started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years. ” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

Diungkapkan bahwa the data-centric ai movement is much bigger than one company or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that showed up.

Berdasarkan laporan, you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?.

Diungkapkan bahwa ng: you hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—i once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

When you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand new model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?.

Berdasarkan laporan, ng: let me describe what landing ai does. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. For big data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. It is a pretrained model. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. Having said that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

Berdasarkan laporan, “collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity. ” —Andrew Ng.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very quickly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

Could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?.

Berdasarkan laporan, ng: very much so. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. New tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an important piece of the puzzle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the powerful tools that data-centric ai gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ng: in ai, data cleaning is important, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention quickly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for example, i once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?.

Berdasarkan laporan, ng: i think synthetic data is an important tool in the tool chest of data-centric ai. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ng: not really. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “in the consumer software internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. ” —Andrew Ng.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that i will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

To make these issues more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a company approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?.

Diungkapkan bahwa ng: when a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the foci of landing ai is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ng: it varies by manufacturer. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. m. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a. Those stable environments make things easier. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and update the model. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the consumer software internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?.

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ng: yes, exactly! this is an industry-wide problem in ai, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent new neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s important for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ng: in the last decade, the biggest shift in ai was a shift to deep learning. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

Diungkapkan bahwa this article appears in the april 2022 print issue as “andrew ng, ai minimalist. ”.

#379. How AI Will Change Chip Design

📅 08 Feb 2022

How AI Will Change Chip Design

Tanggal: 08 Feb 2022 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-chip-design-matlab

Artificial intelligence’s promise and potential for the semiconductor industry.

Rina Diane Caballar is a contributing editor covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment.

An array of semiconductor wafers are ready to be made into chips.

Diungkapkan bahwa the end of moore’s law is looming. Engineers and designers can do only so much to miniaturize transistors and pack as many of them as possible into chips. So they’re turning to other approaches to chip design, incorporating technologies like AI into the process.

Sebagaimana diketahui, samsung, for instance, is adding ai to its memory chips to enable processing in memory, thereby saving energy and speeding up machine learning. Speaking of speed, Google’s TPU V4 AI chip has doubled its processing power compared with that of its previous version.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but ai holds still more promise and potential for the semiconductor industry. To better understand how AI is set to revolutionize chip design, we spoke with Heather Gorr, senior product manager for MathWorks’ MATLAB platform.

How is AI currently being used to design the next generation of chips?.

Berdasarkan laporan, heather gorr: ai is such an important technology because it’s involved in most parts of the cycle, including the design and manufacturing process. There’s a lot of important applications here, even in the general process engineering where we want to optimize things. I think defect detection is a big one at all phases of the process, especially in manufacturing. But even thinking ahead in the design process, [AI now plays a significant role] when you’re designing the light and the sensors and all the different components. There’s a lot of anomaly detection and fault mitigation that you really want to consider.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then, thinking about the logistical modeling that you see in any industry, there is always planned downtime that you want to mitigate; but you also end up having unplanned downtime. So, looking back at that historical data of when you’ve had those moments where maybe it took a bit longer than expected to manufacture something, you can take a look at all of that data and use AI to try to identify the proximate cause or to see something that might jump out even in the processing and design phases. We think of AI oftentimes as a predictive tool, or as a robot doing something, but a lot of times you get a lot of insight from the data through AI.

What are the benefits of using AI for chip design?.

Diungkapkan bahwa gorr: historically, we’ve seen a lot of physics-based modeling, which is a very intensive process. You could create a surrogate model, so to speak, of that physics-based model, use the data, and then do your parameter sweeps, your optimizations, your Monte Carlo simulations using the surrogate model. We want to do a reduced order model, where instead of solving such a computationally expensive and extensive model, we can do something a little cheaper. That takes a lot less time computationally than solving the physics-based equations directly. So, we’re seeing that benefit in many ways, including the efficiency and economy that are the results of iterating quickly on the experiments and the simulations that will really help in the design.

So it’s like having a digital twin in a sense?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, gorr: exactly. That’s pretty much what people are doing, where you have the physical system model and the experimental data. Then, in conjunction, you have this other model that you could tweak and tune and try different parameters and experiments that let sweep through all of those different situations and come up with a better design in the end.

So, it’s going to be more efficient and, as you said, cheaper?.

Diungkapkan bahwa gorr: yeah, definitely. That’s obviously going to yield dramatic cost savings if you’re actually manufacturing and producing [the chips]. Especially in the experimentation and design phases, where you’re trying different things. You want to simulate, test, experiment as much as possible without making something using the actual process engineering.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’ve talked about the benefits. How about the drawbacks?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gorr: the [ai-based experimental models] tend to not be as accurate as physics-based models. Of course, that’s why you do many simulations and parameter sweeps. But that’s also the benefit of having that digital twin, where you can keep that in mind—it’s not going to be as accurate as that precise model that we’ve developed over the years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, both chip design and manufacturing are system intensive; you have to consider every little part. And that can be really challenging. It’s a case where you might have models to predict something and different parts of it, but you still need to bring it all together.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the other things to think about too is that you need the data to build the models. You have to incorporate data from all sorts of different sensors and different sorts of teams, and so that heightens the challenge.

How can engineers use AI to better prepare and extract insights from hardware or sensor data?.

Diungkapkan bahwa gorr: we always think about using ai to predict something or do some robot task, but you can use ai to come up with patterns and pick out things you might not have noticed before on your own. People will use AI when they have high-frequency data coming from many different sensors, and a lot of times it’s useful to explore the frequency domain and things like data synchronization or resampling. Those can be really challenging if you’re not sure where to start.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the things i would say is, use the tools that are available. I think many of us are buried in data and just not sure what to do with it, so definitely take advantage of what’s already out there in the community. There’s a vast community of people working on these things, and you can find lots of examples [of applications and techniques] on GitHub or MATLAB Central, where people have shared nice examples, even little apps they’ve created. You can explore and see what makes sense to you, and bring in that balance of domain knowledge and the insight you get from the tools and AI.

What should engineers and designers consider when using AI for chip design?.

Diungkapkan bahwa gorr: think through what problems you’re trying to solve or what insights you might hope to find, and try to be clear about that. Consider all of the different components, and document and test each of those different parts. Consider all of the people involved, and explain and hand off in a way that is sensible for the whole team.

How do you think AI will affect chip designers’ jobs?.

Diungkapkan bahwa gorr: it’s going to free up a lot of human capital for more advanced tasks. We can use AI to reduce waste, to optimize the materials, to optimize the design, but then you still have that human involved whenever it comes to decision-making. I think it’s a great example of people and technology working hand in hand. It’s also an industry where all people involved—even on the manufacturing floor—need to have some level of understanding of what’s happening, so this is a great industry for advancing AI because of how we test things and how we think about them before we put them on the chip.

How do you envision the future of AI and chip design?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gorr: it’s very much dependent on that human element—involving people in the process and having that interpretable model. We can do many things with the mathematical minutiae of modeling, but it comes down to how people are using it, how everybody in the process is understanding and applying it. Communication and involvement of people of all skill levels in the process are going to be really important. We’re going to see less of those superprecise predictions and more transparency of information, sharing, and that digital twin—not only using AI but also using our human knowledge and all of the work that many people have done over the years.

Berdasarkan laporan, rina diane caballar is a writer covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment. An IEEE Spectrum contributing editor, she's a former software engineer based in New Zealand.

#380. WhatsApp may soon replace the Communities tab on iOS

📅 11 Nov 2026

WhatsApp may soon replace the Communities tab on iOS

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/11/whatsapp-may-soon-replace-the-communities-tab-on-ios/

Berdasarkan laporan, some whatsapp beta testers on ios are seeing a new option in the app’s bottom navigation bar that replaces the communities tab. Here are the details.

Over the past few years, WhatsApp has increasingly focused on Communities as more people have turned to messaging platforms to interact in smaller, more private groups rather than through traditional social networks.

At the same time, WhatsApp has been testing several features that make it easier for users to see which of their contacts are online and available to chat.

Back in May, WABetaInfo found that WhatsApp was developing a new Contacts hub that would bring together users’ favorite contacts, as well as those who were currently online or had recently been active.

A few weeks later, WhatsApp began testing a new green dot indicator on iOS to make it easier to identify contacts who were online.

Now, WABetaInfo reports that WhatsApp is rolling out the new Contacts hub to some iOS beta testers, replacing the Communities tab in the app’s bottom navigation bar.

Diungkapkan bahwa the new tab includes a section with favorite contacts and a full contact list. WhatsApp marks these contacts with a green dot, so users can easily distinguish them from offline contacts. Users can see their favorite contacts at the top of the screen, making it easier to start a conversation with them. They can also sort the full contact list by activity, alphabetical, and birthdays. With alphabetical, the app organizes contacts by name. WhatsApp also sorts recently active contacts by last seen, so users can quickly identify who was active most recently. With activity, WhatsApp shows who is currently online at the top of the list. With birthdays, WhatsApp sorts contacts by their upcoming birthday, so users can see who has a birthday coming up soon.

The site notes that the new tab also allows users to add contacts directly, with the option to sync them to their iPhone’s address book.

As for Communities, the feature itself isn’t going away, but rather being moved to a dedicated filter in the Chats tab.

WABetaInfo also notes that WhatsApp is experimenting with potentially replacing the Updates tab, rather than Communities, with the Contacts tab in a future configuration.

For now, the new Contacts tab is available to a limited number of beta testers running the latest WhatsApp beta for iOS via TestFlight, with a broader rollout expected over the coming weeks.

#385. Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

📅 07 Feb 2022

Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

Tanggal: 07 Feb 2022 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/2d-hbn-qubit

MIT researchers use 2D materials for capacitors in quantum circuits in an effort to scale processors.

Superconducting quantum processor and its microwave packaging.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, quantum computing is a devilishly complex technology, with many technical hurdles impacting its development. Of these challenges two critical issues stand out: miniaturization and qubit quality.

Berdasarkan laporan, ibm has adopted the superconducting qubit road map of reaching a 1,121-qubit processor by 2023, leading to the expectation that 1,000 qubits with today’s qubit form factor is feasible. However, current approaches will require very large chips (50 millimeters on a side, or larger) at the scale of small wafers, or the use of chiplets on multichip modules. While this approach will work, the aim is to attain a better path toward scalability.

Berdasarkan laporan, now researchers at mit have been able to both reduce the size of the qubits and done so in a way that reduces the interference that occurs between neighboring qubits. The MIT researchers have increased the number of superconducting qubits that can be added onto a device by a factor of 100.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we are addressing both qubit miniaturization and quality,” said william oliver, the director for the center for quantum engineering at mit. Sacrificing performance for qubit number is not a useful trade in quantum computing. “Unlike conventional transistor scaling, where only the number really matters, for qubits, large numbers are not sufficient, they must also be high-performance. They must go hand in hand. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the key to this big increase in qubit density and reduction of interference comes down to the use of two-dimensional materials, in particular the 2d insulator hexagonal boron nitride (hbn). The MIT researchers demonstrated that a few atomic monolayers of hBN can be stacked to form the insulator in the capacitors of a superconducting qubit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, just like other capacitors, the capacitors in these superconducting circuits take the form of a sandwich in which an insulator material is sandwiched between two metal plates. 02 degrees above absolute zero (-273. The big difference for these capacitors is that the superconducting circuits can operate only at extremely low temperatures—less than 0. 15 °C).

Berdasarkan laporan, superconducting qubits are measured at temperatures as low as 20 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator. Nathan Fiske/MIT.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in that environment, insulating materials that are available for the job, such as pe-cvd silicon oxide or silicon nitride, have quite a few defects that are too lossy for quantum computing applications. To get around these material shortcomings, most superconducting circuits use what are called coplanar capacitors. In these capacitors, the plates are positioned laterally to one another, rather than on top of one another.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a result, the intrinsic silicon substrate below the plates and to a smaller degree the vacuum above the plates serve as the capacitor dielectric. Intrinsic silicon is chemically pure and therefore has few defects, and the large size dilutes the electric field at the plate interfaces, all of which leads to a low-loss capacitor. The lateral size of each plate in this open-face design ends up being quite large (typically 100 by 100 micrometers) in order to achieve the required capacitance.

In an effort to move away from the large lateral configuration, the MIT researchers embarked on a search for an insulator that has very few defects and is compatible with superconducting capacitor plates.

“We chose to study hBN because it is the most widely used insulator in 2D material research due to its cleanliness and chemical inertness,” said colead author Joel Wang, a research scientist in the Engineering Quantum Systems group of the MIT Research Laboratory for Electronics.

Berdasarkan laporan, on either side of the hbn, the mit researchers used the 2d superconducting material, niobium diselenide. One of the trickiest aspects of fabricating the capacitors was working with the niobium diselenide, which oxidizes in seconds when exposed to air, according to Wang. This necessitates that the assembly of the capacitor occur in a glove box filled with argon gas.

While this would seemingly complicate the scaling up of the production of these capacitors, Wang doesn’t regard this as a limiting factor.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what determines the quality factor of the capacitor are the two interfaces between the two materials,” said wang. “Once the sandwich is made, the two interfaces are “sealed” and we don’t see any noticeable degradation over time when exposed to the atmosphere. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this lack of degradation is because around 90 percent of the electric field is contained within the sandwich structure, so the oxidation of the outer surface of the niobium diselenide does not play a significant role anymore. This ultimately makes the capacitor footprint much smaller, and it accounts for the reduction in cross talk between the neighboring qubits.

“The main challenge for scaling up the fabrication will be the wafer-scale growth of hBN and 2D superconductors like [niobium diselenide], and how one can do wafer-scale stacking of these films,” added Wang.

Diungkapkan bahwa wang believes that this research has shown 2d hbn to be a good insulator candidate for superconducting qubits. He says that the groundwork the MIT team has done will serve as a road map for using other hybrid 2D materials to build superconducting circuits.

Dexter Johnson is a contributing editor at IEEE Spectrum, with a focus on nanotechnology.

Google DeepMind Staff Tap the UK Government to Escalate Their Unionization Fight

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/google-deepmind-staff-escalate-their-union-fight/

Google DeepMind employees in the UK have asked the government to intervene in a push to unionize the artificial intelligence lab.

On Thursday, the Communication Workers Union and Unite the Union—put forward by Google DeepMind staff as joint representatives—filed an application with the Central Arbitration Committee, a government body that resolves disputes between employers and unions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the application, which was seen by wired, asks the cac to confirm that the unions have enough support from workers to trigger a unionization ballot. The company would be required by law to respect the results. If successful, roughly 1,000 staff working in product-focused roles at Google DeepMind would qualify for union membership.

The escalation follows a series of meetings between employees, the unions, and company representatives over voluntary unionization, which left staff with the impression that their demands weren’t being taken seriously.

Diungkapkan bahwa “they’ve been ignored. “Management has refused to come to the table. They feel like their problems have been minimized,” John Chadfield, national officer for technology at the CWU, tells WIRED. They sent it to the HR and labor relations people, who dealt with it as an administrative box-ticking exercise. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we respect the right of employees to make an informed decision about whether or not to join a union,” google deepmind spokesperson tom hewett tells wired in a statement. “We have consistently listened to both those seeking to unionize and those opposed, and have acted in good faith from the outset. We remain committed to constructively participating in this process, and have maintained open and transparent communication with our employees and the unions throughout. ”.

The push to unionize began in February 2025, when Alphabet, Google’s parent company, removed a pledge from its ethics guidelines stating that it wouldn’t use AI for purposes like weapons development.

Berdasarkan laporan, “when i joined, we really made a big deal about the principles—the red lines. “A lot of this is about reestablishing that ethical and moral framework that we started with. We were really looking to benefit humanity and make the world a better place,” a Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for fear of backlash, tells WIRED. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the employees pushing for unionization object in particular to agreements between the company and the us and israeli militaries. If they succeed in unionizing, they intend to demand that Google backs out of those contracts.

“We feel extremely concerned about the direction that this technology is going in,” says a second Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for the same reason as the first employee.

The company has previously defended its deals with government organizations.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we are proud to be part of a broad consortium of leading ai labs and technology and cloud companies providing ai services and infrastructure in support of national security,” jenn crider, a google spokeswoman, told the new york times in april. “We remain committed to the private and public sector consensus that AI should not be used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weaponry without appropriate human oversight. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in an email delivered to all uk staff on thursday, seen by wired, the google deepmind employees involved in the unionization push appealed to their colleagues to participate in the ballot, which they expect to take place in the coming months. “We want a union, we want collective bargaining, and we want a say in how AI is developed and deployed,” they wrote.

The group also hopes it can establish a playbook that employees at other major AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic can follow in the UK.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s pretty rare that there’s been an industry that exercises such dominance and power over the economy, where there’s so little opportunity for employees or regulators to have any checks and balances,” the second google deepmind employee says. “We want to show what can happen when employees collectively organize and articulate a shared vision for the way their technology should be used. ”.

#388. 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/gta-6-runs-best-on-playstation-5-consoles?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, grand theft auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for gta 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation playstation or xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027. ) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rockstar confirmed as much in a post on tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, no matter which console you play gta 6 on, rockstar says that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to that point, rockstar called out the ps5 pro specifically in its post, announcing, "the playstation 5 pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through playstation spectral super resolution (pssr) and ray-traced shadows only available on playstation 5 pro. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, pssr is sony's ai upscaler, similar to options like dlss from nvidia, which uses ai to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

Berdasarkan laporan, while playstation and xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only ps5 pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and ai upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the post, rockstar also announced that the ps5 version of gta 6 takes advantage of other playstation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the dualsense controller, spatial audio rendering using the playstation's tempest 3d audio, as well as improved load times—though rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

Berdasarkan laporan, that's not to say that microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Berdasarkan laporan, again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for gta 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

Diungkapkan bahwa inlining isn't a cause: relax inlines more than rustc does. Every row is a work item.

Relax is for development iteration: release builds use rustc.

Sebagaimana diketahui, relax owns the whole pipeline, from source bytes to executable memory, in one process. It is a stack of layers, each its own crate, building only on the ones below; the layers compile in parallel, and a change in an upper layer never rebuilds the ones below.

Diungkapkan bahwa a function's life. The first call of a function compiles it (interpreter or O1); while it is hot, it is recompiled at O3 in the background and swapped in. Before main, the program's own crates are type-checked. When you save a change to it, Relax rechecks what changed, recompiles it and publishes the new code; the old code stays valid, and the next call runs the new function.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, design rules. Code only grows: published machine code is never freed or rewritten while it can still be on a stack, so a swap is safe where a native hot-reload hack isn't. Never stale: every cached result is keyed by the hashes of its inputs. Lazy by default: Relax compiles what you call, not everything you might. Inspectable: every phase reports what it's doing, so a stall can be explained from its record.

Diungkapkan bahwa the compiler is the relax_compiler library (cargo build --release -p relax-compiler); relax (tools/run/runner) is its command-line runner. Building it needs a stable Rust toolchain and nothing from crates. io.

How to clean a stainless steel sink and bring back its showroom shine using basic cupboard staples.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you are getting your home ready for festive hosting, do not overlook the sink. Even with pristine worktops and clean floors, cloudy stainless steel covered in chalky water rings instantly makes a kitchen feel tired.

Diungkapkan bahwa before the holiday cooking frenzy begins, you can revive a dull basin without scratching the metal or buying pricey specialty cleaners. This five-minute routine cuts through greasy buildup and seals in a bright, showroom shine just in time for visitors.

Berdasarkan laporan, rinse away loose food debris, then wash the entire basin thoroughly with hot water and dish soap. Using a soft microfiber cloth or non-scratch sponge, wipe in long, steady strokes that follow the faint brushed grain of the steel rather than scrubbing in circles.

This removes the surface grease film so your cleaning paste can make direct contact with the mineral spots underneath.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sprinkle a light dusting of baking soda over the damp steel, concentrating on the drain and faucet base where hard water residue gathers. Using a damp cloth, work the powder into a paste along the metal's grain to lift dull water rings without scratching.

For stubborn hard-water marks, rinse the baking soda paste away thoroughly first, then apply a light spray of white vinegar directly to the mineral scale.

Letting the vinegar sit undiluted for a few minutes allows its mild acetic acid to chemically dissolve crusty calcium and magnesium deposits without being neutralized by the alkaline baking soda.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Avoid spraying vinegar onto specialized faucet finishes like matte black, brass, or oil-rubbed bronze, as the acid can strip or discolor the coating.

Once the mineral scale softens, use a soft-bristled brush or non-scratch sponge to gently agitate and lift any remaining gritty buildup from the metal’s surface texture.

Diungkapkan bahwa standing water left to evaporate is why cloudy spots return. Use a dry dish towel or microfiber cloth to wipe the entire basin, faucet, and drainboard until completely dry.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for an optional finishing shine, apply a single drop of mineral oil (like baby oil) or olive oil to a soft cloth and buff it into the steel, following the direction of the metal's grain. Buff vigorously with a clean, dry section of the towel until no residue remains.

This creates a light barrier that repels water beads and keeps the shine lasting longer, especially on faucets and handles.

‘Heartland’ shows the less glamorous side of fame.

Berdasarkan laporan, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a country music superstar, a missing rising star and the darker side of nashville make for an intriguing setup, especially when you’ve got an oscar-winning actress leading the investigation. That's the premise behind “Heartland,” Netflix's latest original thriller, starring Jessica Chastain as a retired country music legend. The film is written and directed by Shana Feste, who previously explored the country music scene in 2010's “Country Strong. ” This time though, she's trading the musical drama for a mystery thriller.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in “heartland,” chastain plays misty jones, a former country music megastar who has spent 20 years away from nashville and the spotlight. Her investigation quickly draws her into Nashville’s murkier corners, where she encounters a number of potential suspects: Charlie’s boyfriend Jace (Ross Lynch) and manager Roy Combs (Garrett Hedlund). However, when her niece Charlie Heart (Carter Faith), an up-and-coming country singer, suddenly goes missing, Misty returns to her old hometown to find her. Along the way, Misty also finds herself confronting some uncomfortable truths about her own past.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve already watched “heartland,” and while its premise certainly caught my attention, i’m not entirely convinced the finished movie delivers everything it promises. So, is this latest Netflix original worth adding to your watchlist, or are we looking at another forgettable thriller from the streamer? Here are my honest thoughts and whether I’d recommend giving it a watch this weekend.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m alix, a lifelong horror nerd who loves watching, reviewing and writing about the latest movies and tv shows. When I’m not working through my ever-growing horror watchlist, I’m covering the biggest releases across streaming and film, including the latest DC movie "Clayface," "VisionQuest" on Disney+, and "The Institute" season 2 on MGM+.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “heartland” gets off to a pretty jarring start, with misty ending up in a heated disagreement with her neighbor over her dogs. I understand what the movie is going for here, using the confrontation to establish Misty’s closed-off nature and aggressive streak, but it’s an unusual way to introduce the character and didn’t immediately win me over. Still, like many of Netflix’s original movies, the first half is where “Heartland” is at its strongest.

Berdasarkan laporan, we get straight into the mystery surrounding charlie’s disappearance, with misty’s brother pleading for her to return to nashville after charlie has missed several shows and concerts, leaving fans to drag her name through the mud online. Chastain gives a strong enough performance, but I struggled to connect with Misty, which made it harder to invest in her personal journey. Returning to her hometown also brings plenty of painful memories to the surface, with quick, scattered flashbacks offering glimpses into the trauma she’s spent years trying to bury. It was the mystery surrounding her niece that kept me interested.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, that mystery doesn’t have quite the staying power the movie needs. Once the reveal comes into focus, there’s very little left to keep you guessing, particularly if you’ve been paying attention to how certain characters are introduced and positioned throughout the opening act. A major twist arrives around the halfway point, and rather than giving the story a much-needed boost, it pretty much sucks the intrigue out of the second half. I had a pretty good idea of where things were heading from early on, so the eventual reveal didn’t carry much of a punch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s a shame, because the first half does enough to make you curious about what’s really going on, but the film struggles to maintain that momentum once its biggest secret is out in the open. That said, “Heartland” does at least make good use of its country music roots, with plenty of on-stage performances and music woven into the story. There’s also an interesting look at the darker side of fame, particularly the pressure of staying relevant and the way public perception can turn against you.

Diungkapkan bahwa sign up to the weekly tom's streaming guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unfortunately, “heartland” is another netflix original that’s likely to be forgotten about before long. The atmosphere, music and locations feel deeply rooted in Nashville’s country music scene, which is arguably where the movie works best. The biggest frustration is that it makes very little effort to deliver a genuinely compelling story, with weak reveals and predictable twists making the climax particularly dull. However, those elements can only do so much when the mystery at the heart of the story is so underwhelming.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’d say “heartland” is worth a watch if you’re a fan of jessica chastain’s work or simply in the mood for some country music and a little nashville drama. However, if you’re looking for a mystery thriller with clever twists, memorable characters and a satisfying payoff, this probably isn’t going to scratch that itch. For the most part, I’d recommend giving this one a miss and saving your Netflix evening for something better.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “this is going to make our spam fighting even worse. This is horrible. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “every decision made by reddit lately encourages spam and/or abuse that will make spam. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “not a single person who uses reddit wants this. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “you are incentivising existing spammers to continue or step up their activities, now that there’s a new well they can poison. ”.

#400. Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

📅 11 Nov 2026

Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/aura-e-ink-picture-frame-review?utm_medium=RSS

Diungkapkan bahwa last year, aura released the aura ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the lcd screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my issues, the new device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, most digital photo frames will remind you of an ipad with a decorative border around it. The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo. You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now for the downsides: where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the aura ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that said, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the new 10-inch model offers some big upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:.

Diungkapkan bahwa resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side. ).

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than aura's most popular offering, the 10. 1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

#401. Synchron Pauses Trials of Its Brain Implant Due to Performance Issues

📅 12 Nov 2026

Synchron Pauses Trials of Its Brain Implant Due to Performance Issues

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/synchron-pauses-trials-of-its-brain-implant-due-to-performance-issues/

Brain implant company Synchron has paused clinical trials of its second-generation device after it failed to perform as expected in initial study participants, WIRED has learned.

The Brooklyn-based startup, a competitor to Elon Musk’s Neuralink, is also undergoing a restructuring, which includes eliminating jobs and scaling back its footprint in New York while building up a team in San Diego to support the development of an entirely new device.

Diungkapkan bahwa synchron is one of several companies developing brain-computer interface technology meant to allow people to control digital devices by reading brain signals and translating those signals into output commands. The company has touted its technology, dubbed the Stentrode, as minimally invasive since it does not rest in the brain itself or require brain surgery.

Berdasarkan laporan, instead, the stent-like mesh tube is inserted into the jugular vein at the base of the neck, then guided with a catheter to sit on top of the brain’s motor cortex. Ten volunteers across the US and Australia received that device and were able to send emails, text, browse the internet, and do online shopping and banking with their thoughts. The company’s first-generation Stentrode connected using an external wire resting on a user’s chest. Synchron has also enabled volunteers to control an Amazon Alexa and Apple’s iPad and Vision Pro without using their hands or voice.

Berdasarkan laporan, synchron’s second-generation device has fewer electrodes and is fully wireless, using bluetooth to connect. The company launched a multisite trial in the US earlier this spring with sister sites in Australia and Canada to evaluate the newer Stentrode, and some participants have already had it implanted. Those sites have recently paused enrollment, however, because the device is not working as intended, according to sources familiar with the trials who asked to remain anonymous.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a statement to wired, synchron says it voluntarily paused enrollment “after identifying a performance issue involving the lead, the cable that carries signals from the stentrode to the implanted electronics. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the issue does not involve the stentrode itself and no safety issues related to the device have been identified. The pause was a company decision, not an FDA-directed action,” the statement continues.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company says it has since brought lead design and manufacturing in-house. Instead of fixing the lead alone, Synchron says it is upgrading the whole Stentrode system and will resume trial enrollment once the hardware upgrades are complete.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we will continue to support participants with stentrode devices across their lifetime. Our commitment to their care and well-being remains unchanged,” Synchron says.

Berdasarkan laporan, two of the five us trial sites that wired was able to reach confirmed that recruitment is on hold at those locations. A coordinator at one site said the pause was not safety-related and was due to Synchron taking a look at the device to make sure the company is getting the readouts it is looking for.

These trials are key to Synchron advancing the Stentrode into a larger pivotal trial, which is needed for the US Food and Drug Administration to grant marketing approval.

“We still have strong confidence that it has the potential to be a first-line therapy,” CEO Tom Oxley says of the Stentrode.

Berdasarkan laporan, synchron’s website and linkedin page show around a dozen job openings in san diego, including electrical and mechanical engineers, microchip designers, and materials scientists. The San Diego team will be designing and manufacturing the upgraded lead and Stentrode, as well as a separate device that the company has not yet revealed that will go “beyond the blood vessels altogether,” according to its website. Oxley previously told WIRED that the company was planning to develop a device that reaches multiple brain regions at once, which could allow more complex and natural functions beyond moving a cursor or making a mouse click.

Berdasarkan laporan, the brain-computer interface field is expanding rapidly, with money pouring into companies pursuing both implanted devices and wearables. Synchron was estimated to have a nearly $1 billion valuation after closing a $200 million funding round last fall. It is backed by Khosla Ventures and the venture firms of Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos.

Diungkapkan bahwa neuralink was reportedly valued as high as $42 billion in secondary market transactions as of this summer. The coin-sized device sits in the skull and has 64 tiny, flexible wires that are threaded into the brain. A few weeks after Arbaugh received the device, several of the wires came out of his brain, leading to a loss of cursor control. The company had an early problem with its implant in 2024 after it malfunctioned in its first volunteer, Noland Arbaugh. Neuralink was able to compensate for the lost threads and restore control by modifying its recording algorithm.

Berdasarkan laporan, recent advances in artificial intelligence are fueling the development of brain-computer interfaces since ai models can read brain patterns faster and more accurately than traditional algorithms. Merge Labs, a brain-computer interface company cofounded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, came out of stealth in January with $252 million in funding. OpenAI provided some of the funding, and the two companies are collaborating on AI models.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while these devices have shown incredible promise for people with severe motor disorders, they remain experimental. Synchron’s setback shows just how far the field still has to go before these systems are commercially available for patients.

At the time of writing, the most recent post was published just 57 minutes earlier, suggesting that Apple only recently disabled new submissions.

9to5Mac has reached out to Apple for comment and clarification on the scope of the shutdown, and we’ll update this story if we hear back.

#410. Best Open Earbuds (2026): Shokz, Bose, Soundcore, and More

📅 18 Sep 2026

Best Open Earbuds (2026): Shokz, Bose, Soundcore, and More

Tanggal: 18 Sep 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, open earbuds are the big new thing in headphone land. Some use a hook style that wraps around the back of your ear, while others are clip-ons that look more like statement-piece earrings. Unlike in-ear variants, open earbuds are like tiny speakers that rest on the ear and let outside sound in naturally, so you can fully hear the world around you. Style aside, they are excellent for anyone who finds traditional earbuds uncomfortable or wants full environmental awareness for activities like running, biking, or even just doing chores around the house.

I’ve tested dozens of models since 2022, and while I still recommend noise-canceling earbuds, I also love open earbuds for specific use cases.

For more headphone recommendations, check out our guides to the Best Wireless Earbuds, Best Workout Headphones, and Best Wireless Headphones.

Diungkapkan bahwa updated november 2026: i am recommending the anker aeroclip 2 as the best overall, followed closely by the shokz opendots. I’ve also added the Apple AirPods 5 and CMF Clip Pro as an honorable mention.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these are truly take-everywhere, do-anything headphones i would recommend to anyone looking for great open earbuds. They are exceedingly comfortable and easy to use all day, so much so that I sometimes forgot I was wearing them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, they’re clip-ons that wrap around the earlobe, with the speaker end resting at the ear canal opening and the other end behind the ear. Importantly, the top of your ear is free for glasses, sunglasses, or hats. Like nearly all open earbuds, they let in sound from your surroundings, so don’t expect them to be a great companion for long-haul flights or daily gym sessions.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are other open earbuds that are nearly as good as these, and some surpass them in areas like sound quality. The physical button controls on each earbud are much easier to use than touch-sensitive alternatives, especially when running or exercising outdoors. But it’s a combination of small details that puts the AeroClip 2 at the top. And, importantly, the call quality is great. The charging case is surprisingly small, smaller than most other options on this list. These buds use the same AI-powered chip as the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro, and while they don’t sound quite as good, they are noticeably better than other open earbuds, especially in noisy environments.

The best part? They cost less than many similar competitors I tested.

Diungkapkan bahwa my former top pick, and still a great option, especially if you value battery life. These earbuds do most of what the Soundcore AeroClip 2 does, just a little larger and a little pricier. The buds are exceedingly comfortable and stable for all-day wear, even during outdoor workouts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what sets them apart from the aeroclip 2 is battery life. They also have an IP57 dust and water-resistance rating, the same as premium, flagship earbuds like Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro. They are best in class—10 hours on a single charge, and 40 hours total with the charging case. I’ve worn them in the rain, on the beach, and fully submerged them in water multiple times without issue.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they are a bit pricey, though. Shokz recently launched the lower-priced Shokz OpenDots Air and Shokz OpenFit Air 2—I may update this recommendation depending on how my testing goes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the bose ultra open earbuds were a big deal when they launched in 2024—a brand-new design from bose and one of the biggest swings from a major brand in clip-on open earbuds. Two years later, the brand launched the second-generation version, and they are a solid, if expensive, option. That’s mainly because of sound quality—these earbuds sound clearer and more defined than most competitors. Another differentiator is physical button controls on each bud, which I find easier to use than touch alternatives, especially when running or biking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like the soundcore and shokz earbuds, they are very comfortable, so much so that i sometimes forgot i am wearing them. They also now support wireless charging, a big omission in the first generation. This gen-two version has a more distinct, two-tone material design that is certainly eye-catching, especially in the white colorway. But they are much pricier by comparison, and only worth it if you want the best sound quality in this clip-on form factor.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it can be a little nerve-wracking to spend big bucks on a concept (open earbuds) you aren’t totally convinced by. That’s one reason I love this $50 option—the PearClip Pros aren’t super pricey and are a great way to find out if you even like open earbuds in the first place, especially the kind that clip onto the outside of your ear.

Diungkapkan bahwa they are far less refined than shokz or soundcore. Things like the app and touch controls can be a little finicky. But that’s common at this super-low price point, and you can always upgrade to a more premium earbud if you fall in love with the clip-on form factor.

Berdasarkan laporan, the shokz openrun pro 2 are more like headphones than earbuds—with a wraparound headband, long battery life, great sound quality (for open headphones), and no charging case. They use a combination of bone conduction (think vibrations) and air conduction (think tiny speakers pointed toward your ears) to deliver clearer sound than most smaller open earbuds, especially in noisy environments. That combination of technologies is why these are some of my favorite earbuds for outdoor fitness activities like running and biking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i do wish these headphones were a little cheaper. I’m currently testing the recently released, more affordable Shokz OpenRun Air 2, and I’m hopeful they can be a budget-friendly alternative.

Berdasarkan laporan, apple airpods 5 with wireless charging case for $149: apple airpods 5 are semi-open earbuds—they still go in your ears, but don’t have rubber eartips that block outside noise, meaning you can still hear the world around you pretty clearly. Because they go in your ear somewhat, they have better sound quality and automated noise-canceling than nearly all of my top picks. Fit, however, is a big issue. While nearly all of my top picks are excellent workout companions, the AirPods 5 are quite the opposite—they can fall out often during exercise and are tricky to control mid-run.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nothing ear (open) for $99: former wired editor adrienne so loves these earbuds and uses them for almost all her outdoor activities. They fit slightly inside your ear and, like most Nothing headphones, have a distinct transparent design. They are very slim (19-mm wide) and lightweight. The case doesn’t clamp shut very firmly, so be careful, but at this price, that’s forgivable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cmf clip pro for $99: if you want something a little nicer and a little more comfortable than our budget pick (the soundpeats pearclip pro), these cmf open earbuds are a solid option. Sure, they’re a big step up in price, but for under $100, I found them more comfortable and easier to use thanks to the physical button control on each earbud (similar to my top picks).

Berdasarkan laporan, jlab epic open sport for $100: jlab’s epic open sport stands out for its controls: the jlab emblem is a touch sensor, and each earbud also has physical buttons on top, making it a breeze to control. What holds the Epic Open Sport back is audio quality—the sound isn’t very detailed and is generally boring to listen to.

Berdasarkan laporan, earfun clip for $70: for around $70, these are a solid pick for anyone on a budget. The problem is our budget pick, the Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, often sells for less and offers a similar overall experience. Former WIRED reviewer Waniata found the overall package punches above its price point, with a snappy, compact case, a comfortable fit, push-button controls, and reliable multi-device Bluetooth connections. Don’t dismiss these earbuds if you find them heavily discounted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shokz openfit pro for $250: the shokz openfit pro has a great premise: open earbuds with noise canceling. And while they do cancel some noise, it’s not much. Hear the world around you as you would without headphones, and turn on noise-canceling when you don’t, just like regular earbuds. The bigger issue is price: for $250, you could get open earbuds and great noise-canceling earbuds that do a better job for each task.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, suunto wing 2 for $179: these open-ear headphones are designed for endurance athletes—they have a long 12-hour battery life and come with a wireless power bank you can take on the go. Dock the headphones in the power bank for up to 36 hours of total battery life. There’s nothing inherently wrong with these headphones, but I don’t see a world where I would recommend them over the Shokz Openrun Pro 2, which retails for the same amount and offers more comfort, a sleeker design, better sound, and a more robust app.

Suunto Spark for $179: The Suunto Spark has a similar story to the Suunto Wing 2: it's built for athletes and syncs with Suunto fitness watches, but the similarly priced Shokz Openfit 2 outclasses it in the areas that matter (comfort, sound quality, battery).

What Are Open Earbuds and How Do They Sound?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at a glance, open earbuds seem a lot like typical wireless earbuds. The big difference is that, instead of going inside your ear canal, they rest somewhere on the outside of your ear, leaving it open so you can easily hear the world around you. I use them all the time for outdoor exercise like running or biking, where I want my music but also need to hear other runners, bikers, and cars to stay safe.

Berdasarkan laporan, because they leave your ears open and the sound comes from farther away (outside your ear rather than inside), audio performance isn’t as clear, intimate, or bassy as regular earbuds. They also typically lack noise-canceling features, so they are not a great fit for the office or air travel.

Sebagaimana diketahui, open earbuds are perfect for outdoor activities or when you want to talk to other people without taking off your headphones. When I run or go for a bike ride, I only use open earbuds so I can hear my surroundings and stay safe. I also like using them around the house when I am cooking or doing laundry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, semi-open earbuds, like apple’s airpods, sit inside the ear but don’t have eartips that create a sound seal. They can offer better audio quality than other open earbuds because the speakers and microphones are closer to your ear and mouth. Semi-open earbuds are comfortable, but they’re usually pretty loose—they can fall out easily and may be a poor option for fitness activities.

Berdasarkan laporan, i test open earbuds like i test any pair of headphones: in the real world, in my daily life. I wear each pair for at least a few weeks to test comfort, battery life, ease of use, and onboard controls. I listen to podcasts, watch TV shows, jam out to my favorite playlists, and call friends.

Diungkapkan bahwa with open earbuds in particular, i also wear them on jogs, bike rides, and errand runs to get a better feel for how stable they are on my ears. I don’t expect them to cancel any noise, so I don’t test them on airplanes or loud commutes—they aren’t really made for that. My main audio source is Spotify Lossless, but, when possible, I test other formats and codecs as well.

#415. iFixit tears down touchscreen MacBook Pro, reveals light-up Apple logo details

📅 10 Nov 2026

iFixit tears down touchscreen MacBook Pro, reveals light-up Apple logo details

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/ifixit-tears-down-touchscreen-macbook-pro-reveals-light-up-apple-logo-details/

Sebagaimana diketahui, ifixit published its teardown of the new macbook pro with proled xdr display today, revealing interesting details about how apple brought back its illuminated logo on the lid. Watch it below.

Diungkapkan bahwa ifixit’s teardown of the new macbook pro with proled xdr display is now live, and it explores not only how the new illuminated apple logo works, but also its tandem oled and how apple managed to trim its weight down to 3 pounds (1. 38 kg) from 3. 4 pounds (1. 55 kg) on the standard 14-inch model.

The teardown opens with a close look at the tandem OLED, which stacks two light-emitting layers to deliver higher brightness than conventional single-layer OLED displays.

Under a microscope, iFixit found that the blue subpixels are larger than the red and green ones, which they say should help reduce strain on the materials and potentially extend the display’s lifespan.

Most of the teardown process is quite familiar from past models, though iFixit noted that replacing the USB-C ports or fans still requires removing the entire logic board, despite both components being independently replaceable.

iFixit noted that the headphone jack also requires logic board removal, while the HDMI port, SDXC port, RAM, and storage remain soldered to the board.

As with past teardowns, iFixit also tested what happens when swapping logic boards between two MacBooks.

While last year’s M5 MacBook Pro failed to complete Touch ID calibration through Apple’s Repair Assistant, iFixit noted that the new model successfully recognized the battery, display, and Touch ID sensor after a logic board swap, with True Tone, brightness controls, and the touchscreen all working as expected.

iFixit was also able to enroll a fingerprint with the donor board installed from another MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

As for the illuminated Apple logo, iFixit had a bit of a rough time getting to it, destroying the OLED panel in the process and even asking whether anyone had managed to remove it intact.

Once inside, iFixit found that the Apple logo is illuminated by a strip of four LEDs, which work in conjunction with a reflective layer and a diffuser to distribute the light evenly.

The Apple logo itself, in turn, has a two-way mirror coating that gives it a shiny, reflective appearance when the LEDs are off, while allowing light to pass through when they’re on.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to weight, apple shaved 92 grams off the chassis and 101 grams off the display assembly, despite adding touch and an illuminated logo. The battery is just 2 grams lighter, while the slightly smaller trackpad saves another 8 grams.

Diungkapkan bahwa finally, ifixit gave the new macbook pro with proled xdr display a repairability score of 5 out of 10. That was one point higher than last year’s M5 MacBook Pro, but one point below the cheaper MacBook Neo.
