#416. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

📅 11 Nov 2026

Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/hackers-now-want-your-browser-sessions-more-than-passwords?utm_medium=RSS

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to threat analysts at darkowl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on russian market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meanwhile, flare research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

Berdasarkan laporan, the easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Diungkapkan bahwa reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Berdasarkan laporan, sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Diungkapkan bahwa change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Diungkapkan bahwa look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

#418. Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia’s New Interim CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026

Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia’s New Interim CEO

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/who-is-colette-kress-the-woman-who-could-succeed-jensen-huang/

Berdasarkan laporan, nvidia’s ceo and cofounder jensen huang is officially out, and longtime chief financial officer colette kress is in. The chipmaker’s board of directors announced Thursday that Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, has been named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman believed by US officials to be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Sebagaimana diketahui, harvey jones, the newly appointed chair of nvidia’s board, said in a statement that kress “has helped lead nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position. ” He added that Kress will be supported by an “experienced leadership team” and that the board has “full confidence” in her.

Kress was among the most obvious candidates to fill the void after Huang’s departure, according to multiple tech executives and industry analysts who follow Nvidia closely, given her long tenure at the company, credibility on Wall Street and across the tech industry, and, perhaps most importantly, her deep familiarity with Nvidia’s business and finances.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she’s extremely strong-willed, professional, and whip-smart. “She obviously has a keen sense for how Jensen thinks. She doesn’t tolerate nonsense. She can be friendly and gracious too,” says a former Nvidia executive who spoke on the condition of anonymity. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “colette is the logical choice,” says patrick moorhead, founder and chief analyst at moor insights & strategies, who has tracked the chip industry for decades. “She has credibility with investors because she answers hard questions directly. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa moorhead says kress has operated as much more than a “numbers” cfo. “In my conversations with her, she goes deep on the product road map, from rack-scale systems to networking and software,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nvidia’s board said on sunday it was launching an independent investigation into huang’s activities following a report by the new york times that he had an affair with a woman named alice huang, who us officials suspected of being a chinese intelligence asset. WIRED reported on Monday that Huang quietly hired a crisis communications firm sometime last year to handle matters related to his personal life. By October of 2025, the firm was being looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang at Nvidia, around the same time The New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether a company linked to Alice Huang had helped Chinese firms evade US chip export controls through its subsidiaries.

Diungkapkan bahwa while huang has long been the public face of nvidia, kress has been responsible for managing the chipmaker’s relationship with wall street. On earnings calls, she often details Nvidia’s financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints, and other key metrics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “one of the things we don’t focus on is the stock price. We focus on our investors and how we would like to innovate,” Kress told the Israeli business newspaper Globes in 2023.

Berdasarkan laporan, before joining nvidia, kress spent more than two decades in finance roles at microsoft, cisco, and texas instruments. Huang personally recruited her in 2013, when Nvidia was still best known for its gaming graphics cards, according to Globes. Huang laid out his vision for the company’s future on a whiteboard, explaining how Nvidia could become a major supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence.

Other potential successors to Huang included Ian Buck, an Nvidia veteran of more than 20 years who created the company’s software platform CUDA and now oversees its high-performance computing business, and Jeff Fisher, who joined Nvidia in 1994 as the head of software sales and later became senior vice president of its GeForce unit, where he led Nvidia’s strategy for bringing GPUs to market.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, nvidia’s unusual corporate structure has long meant that dozens of executives reported directly to huang. The company lacks a traditional chief operating officer. Even executive vice presidents aren’t necessarily given direct control over budgets, sources have told WIRED. As a result, few people within the organization have the same level of understanding of the company’s financials as Kress.

Berdasarkan laporan, the former nvidia executive who spoke to wired on the condition of anonymity said that while kress is incredibly sharp and “can step into the [ceo] role immediately without needing any guidance,” she doesn’t have the same engineering and technical expertise that huang brought to the role. She has also shied away from being “at the center of public attention,” the person said.

Given the intense scrutiny surrounding Huang lately, that leadership style might be a welcome temporary change for Nvidia.

#422. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

📅 10 Nov 2026

Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/why-websites-show-wrong-server-location-when-you-use-vpn?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are many reasons why someone might use a vpn, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you connect to a vpn server in the united states, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the u. S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U. S. S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you’ve encountered something similar with your vpn provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ip geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99. 8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, websites can also use more than just your ip address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, webrtc is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the catch with webrtc is that it exposes both your vpn server and isp-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real ip location and cause websites to reject your vpn server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even when a browser isn’t leaking your real ip address, dns resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you toggle on dns leak protection in your vpn app, this will force websites to use your vpn’s resolver to perform dns lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, websites rely on ip databases like maxmind, ip2location, ipinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Diungkapkan bahwa even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vpn providers often rely on virtual servers that use ip addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

Diungkapkan bahwa while this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Berdasarkan laporan, before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your ip address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a webrtc or dns issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ll start by recording your baseline ip address, country, city, and asn. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig. co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now connect your vpn server. Then visit IPConfig. co again to note down the changed details.

Berdasarkan laporan, make sure the country and timezone fields match your current vpn server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in case these details do not match your vpn server, run a webrtc leak test and a dns leak test using browserleaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s no surefire way to solve ip location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/apple-to-investigate-accident-that-killed-three-workers-at-iphone-parts-factory-in-india/

Since Apple began diversifying its manufacturing operations away from China, India has emerged as a major production hub, with roughly a quarter of the world’s iPhones now manufactured in the country.

Earlier this year, Apple found itself linked to an environmental controversy in India, after the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board investigated allegations that wastewater from a Tata facility had contaminated nearby farmland water.

A few weeks later, however, Tata said the regulator had dropped further action against the facility after the company addressed the concerns raised.

At the time, Tata said it had ordered separate testing related to the facility and that the results supported its position that the plant was operating within the rules.

However, the matter was apparently not fully resolved, as just three days later, Reuters reported that local health officials were still investigating complaints from nearby farmers.

And while there had been no major developments reported about the wastewater investigation since then, Reuters reported today that three contract workers died in an accident at the same Tata facility.

The three contract workers died during maintenance work on an effluent treatment ​plant operated by Nalco Water at the Tata facility, which is located in Hosur in Tamil Nadu, ​district official Dinesh Kumar said, adding that the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank.

Reuters added that “Apple’s team is visiting ​the plant to assist in ​the ongoing investigation,” though the company did not respond when reached for comment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the report added that tata and tamil nadu authorities are also investigating the fatal accident, and noted that “production was not affected as the facility was closed for the hindu festival of deepavali this week. ”.

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://github.com/jjba23/sift

Lisp, Scheme and Emacs Lisp formatter, linter and LSP (language server).

an idempotent formatter, a rule-based linter and a language server for Scheme, Emacs Lisp and Common Lisp.

Diungkapkan bahwa sift reads a lisp source file, reports what is ill-formed in it, and rewrites its whitespace. The rewrite is a total function on text and a fixed point: formatting a formatted file returns it unchanged, and a comment, a blank line, a #; datum comment or a #. read-time form appears in the output in the place it was in the input. Both properties are asserted over every fixture in the suite, so neither is a promise that expires quietly.

Berdasarkan laporan, three dialects are read, each by the rules of its own report rather than by a compromise between them: scheme, emacs lisp and common lisp. A square bracket is a vector in one of them and a clause in the next, and sift does not average the two.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, install it with guix install sift or nix run, or clone the repository and run. The implementation is Guile 3. /bin/sift version. 0 and the standard library, with no C dependency and no build step, because a Scheme program has none; sift doctor reports the interpreter it runs on, the library it loaded and the rules it found.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the same program is a language server (sift lsp). The findings, the fixes and the formatting are computed once and delivered either as text on standard output or as LSP responses, so Emacs through Eglot, Neovim and any other client of the protocol are told exactly what a pipeline is told.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it ships as one executable and one emacs package, under the mit license. The premise is the ordinary one: a Lisp program is a datum with a read syntax, and a formatter that treats it as such can be exact and cheap at the same time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, check, format, lint. The editor and the pipeline receive these same answers. sift check prints the patch it would make and exits 1; sift format prints the formatted file; sift lint names the rule that fired, its severity and its position. Every line in that recording is real output, on files small enough to read in the picture.

Lossless rewriting is the whole of the argument, and the rest follows from it: a diff whose hunks are the change, a fix that replaces one range, a rule that can be silenced without editing the code it objects to.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one decision carries most of the list: a lisp file is read as a tree of forms carrying source positions, not as lines of text, and the formatter prints that tree back. Preservation, a fix that replaces one range, and a diff whose hunks are the change all follow from it. That the reader and the printer are inverse operations is the oldest property Lisp has; the work here is to keep them inverse while the whitespace moves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, guile 3. 0 is the only requirement. The launcher inside a checkout runs the program, so a clone is enough:.

Diungkapkan bahwa check returns 0 if the formatting is good. If not, it prints a patch to stdout and returns 1. It never modifies your files.

Berdasarkan laporan, each line has the shape file:line:column: severity: [rule] sentence, which a compilation buffer, a ci log and grep already parse. Suggestions are findings too, and a deeply nested body is reported rather than rewritten:.

To read what a rule means, ask the program that holds it:.

When the tool and the environment disagree about what is running, the program can be asked what it sees:.

Diungkapkan bahwa two further commands follow from the same records. fix applies the fixes the rules can state as equivalences and reports what remains:.

Diungkapkan bahwa it does not reformat, because formatting belongs to format, and a fix that moved whitespace would touch every line of the patch it was meant to make readable. It does tidy imports: the unused ones are removed and the specifications are sorted, both on by default, and optimize-imports or sort-imports in sift. yaml turns either off. ci is the same pair of questions asked by a pipeline, in one command and one status:.

Diungkapkan bahwa at run time sift needs guile 3. 0 or newer and nothing else. Emacs is optional, and only for the editor half.

The language server asks whichever of guild, emacs and sbcl is installed for its second opinion on a buffer; a compiler that is not present is simply not asked, and compiler-diagnostics: false turns the second opinion off.

Diungkapkan bahwa sift runs on linux and macos. cache/sift elsewhere. Caches follow the platform: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/sift when it is set, /Library/Caches/sift on macOS, and $XDG_CACHE_HOME/sift or /. The optional tools above are found on PATH; a missing one is reported and the feature that needed it is skipped, rather than the tool refusing to run.

No C dependency and no build step are involved, and no package manager sits in the path: the program is Scheme source, loaded by whichever Guile is present.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bin/sift is a small posix shell launcher: it resolves its own symlink chain, puts the sibling src/ on guile’s load path (or $sift_load_path, if one is set), and hands the arguments to (sift cli). Where the launcher is not wanted, the program reduces to this:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, run with guile_load_path pointing at src/. For a prefix, maak install copies the library to $(prefix)/share/guile/site/3. 0 and the launcher to $(prefix)/bin; PREFIX=/usr/local is the default and maak uninstall is its inverse.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the first run guile compiles the library and prints a few ;;; note:. lines to standard error while it does. That is Guile’s auto-compilation, not sift: it stops once the cache is warm, and GUILE_AUTO_COMPILE=0 suppresses it.

From a checkout, the shell command builds the package it ships:.

To install it as a package, the guix-jointhefreeworld channel carries it:.

Berdasarkan laporan, the split between runtime and build inputs is deliberate. sift is a library plus a launcher, and needs only Guile. The repository carries its own derivation, so Nix does not need a second expression to build it:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the flake builds on linux and on macos (x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin), because the closure is guile and scheme and nothing else: on a mac, nix run github:jjba23/sift is the shortest route to a formatter that runs. The image is the one output that is Linux only, and on Darwin it is absent rather than broken.

Diungkapkan bahwa the nix-jointhefreeworld flake carries the same package, built from this repository’s own default. nix:.

Berdasarkan laporan, the image holds debian’s guile, the library and the launcher, and nothing else: there is no build step inside it, because a scheme program has none. Build it from the checkout, or pull it:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the container’s working directory is /src, so a volume mounted there is the tree sift reads; the entry point is sift itself, so the arguments after the image are sift’s arguments. A whole-project run, a patch, a lint and the language server (on standard input and output) all work the same way:.

Diungkapkan bahwa maak package-docker is the first command with the tags already on, and maak push-docker-latest / maak push-docker-tag publish it — the same three tasks maak’s own file has. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a container exists for the other end of the pipe. On macOS no Guile is present that a script can rely on, and no Guix; Docker Desktop is. One image that runs, with a test over it, is cheaper than three install procedures that would each have to be verified on their own.

Diungkapkan bahwa emacs/sift. el is a single file with no dependencies beyond Emacs 28. 1:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the file carries the headers a package needs, so m-x package-install-file on emacs/sift. el also works, for a copy that should live in package-user-dir.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what is enabled after that is a matter for the project. The Emacs chapter has the two arrangements, with and without Eglot, and the settings that can be changed.

Diungkapkan bahwa every command, every option and every exit code is in doc/cli. org, which is the reference. In brief: sift format, sift lint and sift check take files or standard input, sift ci is check and lint in one command for a pipeline, and the status is 0 for clean, 1 for findings and 2 for a usage error or a file that cannot be read.

The determination is an ordered sequence of tests, and the first that answers wins:.

An editor that has already resolved the language is better informed than any of this: the language server takes the identifier the client sends (scheme, emacs-lisp, lisp) and goes by that.

Diungkapkan bahwa the formatter normalises line endings and spacing, places closing delimiters, computes indentation, aligns contiguous inline comments when asked, and preserves blank lines up to the limits of the style. doc/formatting. Nothing else is touched: the position of a line break, the contents of a string and the spelling of an escape belong to the author. The function is deterministic and idempotent, and the suite formats every fixture twice to establish it. org is the page: the two styles, the three indentation rules, every dialect’s read syntax, and the four things it will not do.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a rule is a record: a name, a code, a description, the dialects it applies to, a severity, a procedure and an example. The catalogue holds 92 of them, listed one by one in doc/rules. doc/linting. org. The driver runs those the dialect selects, adds the reader’s own findings, applies the suppression comments, and emits the result in source order. org covers the rest: what a fix may touch, why a fix is discarded rather than guessed at, and how a rule is silenced for a line or for a form.

Berdasarkan laporan, the style is not an invention: it is the common practice of the three lisp communities, written down where it can be argued with. doc/style. org is the long form – each choice, the alternative it beat and the reason – including which of Riastradh’s rules sift keeps and what it declines, the Emacs Lisp conventions that are really byte-compiler warnings, the reasons Common Lisp keeps its closers, and the square bracket a Scheme cond clause is written with. The settings a project is likely to hold differently are listed in the configuration page: a project that has settled a convention should not have to argue with its formatter about it.

Berdasarkan laporan, emacs/sift. It requires Emacs 28. 1 or newer and no external package. There are two ways in – Flymake for the rules, Eglot for the code actions – and doc/emacs. el is a thin package: Emacs carries the text to the executable and the findings back, and every decision stays in one place. org is the page: the Flymake backend and its keymap, Eglot and the code actions, every setting in the customization group, and why sift and TAB can disagree about a third-party macro.

Berdasarkan laporan, anything that speaks lsp can have the server, and anything that reads a compiler’s output can have the program. doc/editors. org carries the details and the recipes, and the ready-made ones live in the repository:.

The human-readable format is file:line:column: severity: [rule] message, which Vim’s :make, Emacs’s compilation-mode and most CI log viewers already parse.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, web/ is the two jobs that are a function of a string — formatting and linting — compiled to webassembly with guile hoot, with an editor page around it. The same reader, the same formatter and all 93 rules run in the tab, and no input leaves it, because there is nowhere for it to go.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is live at https://jointhefreeworld. org/sift/: an editor on a page, with the dialect, the style and the severity as controls, the findings in a panel that links back to the source, an outline, a completion popup, inlay hints that name a call’s arguments, and a rules browser built from the same catalogue the command line prints.

Diungkapkan bahwa the evident way to put a lisp formatter in a browser is to write it again in javascript, and that is a second formatter, which is a second style: the two agree until the first file that exercises them, at which point the project has to decide which of its own tools it believes. The source of truth therefore stayed where it was. The tab runs the reader, the formatter, the lint driver and every rule that bin/sift runs, because they are the same modules.

The whole contract between the page and the Scheme is one procedure of one string to one string:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, everything the tab can do is that procedure: format, check, lint, fix, the rule catalogue, and the four editor questions (hover, go to definition, completion, outline), which are answered by the language server’s own analysis code against an empty workspace. Everything it cannot do requires a filesystem — no directory to walk, no sift. yaml, no save, no server — and the page reports nothing there rather than guessing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hoot compiles r7rs and a subset of guile, and the gap between that and what sift uses is web/compat/. Four Guile libraries have stand-ins: format, textual-ports, threads (a tab is one thread, so (sift pool) takes its sequential path) and ftw (scandir answers nothing, because there are no directories to walk — which is the truth about a tab and not a guess).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the demanding case was srfi-13. scm is written with a re-export Hoot does not implement — so a browser build that reached for it would compile a re-export of names the target does not define and stop there. Twenty-six files in the core import it, Hoot ships srfi-9, srfi-11 and srfi-14 and no SRFI-13, and Guile’s own srfi/srfi-13. The answer is a stand-in of thirteen procedures, written against (scheme base), and a test that runs the browser’s copy in a second process and fails unless its format, lint and fix answers are byte for byte the answers Guile’s library gives. A stand-in that is never compared is a second implementation with no reason to agree with the first.

Four things could not be shimmed, and the source changed instead, in ways that leave a native build no worse off: (sift strings) carries the four string procedures R7RS leaves out, rather than importing a library the target may not have; three (char-set …) call sites became predicates, because a character set is an object R7RS does not have; one procedure takes its port in the body rather than as a keyword default that would be evaluated for nothing; and the filesystem question in (sift imports) asks whether this Scheme has stat and scandir rather than who is compiling it.

Berdasarkan laporan, nothing in src/sift/ names the browser, wasm or hoot. The dependency runs one way, and eight tests hold it that way: the core does not know that a tab exists; the facade’s dependency on the core is still five modules; every Guile library in the compiled closure has a stand-in; the SRFI-13 stand-in is the file a build finds; it answers what Guile’s own library answers, measured in a second process; the page names no URL from the root of a site; every URL it names carries the build stamp; and the editor asks for the wasm beside itself rather than at the root.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the module is 2. 3 MB, which is a formatter, a linter and 93 rules on a Wasm GC — a large page by the standards of a web page and a small one by the standards of an editor. Speed is the part of the experiment with numbers attached:.

Diungkapkan bahwa a screenful falls below the 300 ms debounce the editor applies to a lint, so the first two rows never reach the reader; past two kilobytes the cost is perceptible. There is no JIT, a record is allocated per node, and the reader allocates four records per character: that is the price of a Scheme on a Wasm GC, not something the facade can tune away. Where it matters, the request takes a checkers list, which is how a page asks for less work.

Berdasarkan laporan, two questions were being asked. Whether a Scheme program of real size — not a toy, but a formatter with a reader of its own and 93 rules — can be compiled into something a tab runs: it can, with the caveats above, and the porting work amounted to one compatibility directory rather than a rewrite. Whether the seam survives contact: it does, and the test that establishes it runs under Guile in the ordinary suite, with no browser and no Wasm runtime involved.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the boundary is where the design is constrained. A tab has a buffer and no project, so two rules cannot fire and report nothing rather than guessing, and the language server is not in the tab at all: it is a process on standard input and output, which a browser is not. The experiment covers the formatter and the linter, and those are most of what a Lisp file needs while it is being written.

Berdasarkan laporan, the build is one command because hoot is not a library sift ships: it is a compiler, needed once and never at run time, and locating it is the only difficulty. org has the long form of that, of the two things the server contributes (a. Hoot’s compiled modules are bytecode, and bytecode belongs to the Guile that compiled it, so guix shell guile guile-hoot yields a toolchain that fails halfway through a compile with an error raised inside Hoot; web/build. web/README. sh therefore compiles a two-line program to establish that its toolchain works, and asks Guix for guile-next guile-hoot when it does not. wasm content type and a trailing-slash redirect) and of the one it imposes (a two-day cache, which is what the build stamp in every URL is for).

Berdasarkan laporan, publishing is a copy into /srv/http/jointhefreeworld. org/sift on the machine that serves, which is how the rest of that site is published: no ssh, no rsync, no server to reload, because a file that is present is a file that is served.

Berdasarkan laporan, the extent of what sift lsp answers – request by request, including the requests it refuses, its code actions and the two limits that accompany them – is in doc/language-server. The limits bear repeating: a reference is matched by name within one dialect, because sift expands no macro and follows no import; and the project is read in the background, so a jump answers from the files read so far instead of waiting for the rest. org. A client that advertises experimental is told how far the reading has got by the sift/indexStatus notification (uninitialized, scanning, indexing, ready); the states, the bounds (100 ms for a jump, 200 ms for a reference search) and the batch size are in While the project is being read.

Diungkapkan bahwa it checks the formatting, then lints, prints both reports in the format it was asked for, and exits 1 if either found something, 2 if a file could not be read or parsed. It never writes and never fixes: a job that edits the tree it is judging is a job whose verdict means nothing.

There is a reusable workflow, so most repositories need one file and no flags:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it annotates the diff with what it found and uploads the sarif document to code scanning, so a finding that was not fixed becomes an alert in the security tab rather than a line in a log that is never scrolled again. The same repository publishes a composite action, for a job that wants sift as one step among its own:.

Spelling the step out is also possible: --format=github writes workflow commands instead of prose, so each finding lands as an annotation on the line of the diff:.

And --format=sarif writes one document for the whole run, which is the shape a code scanning service consumes:.

Diungkapkan bahwa the hook runs whichever sift is on path; set sift in the hook’s environment to name another copy. The pre-commit framework is also supported:. pre-commit-hooks. yaml declares three hooks — sift-format (rewrites), sift-check (fails) and sift-lint — so a project selects the one it needs:.

Diungkapkan bahwa a run over a project is a sequence of runs over single files, and the files are independent, so lint, format, check and ci distribute them over the processors and print the answers in file order: a parallel run writes exactly the bytes a sequential run writes. SIFT_JOBS is the only setting involved, and the two runs that are never parallel are the ones that write the files they read. The setting, the two exceptions and the reason the output is ordered are in doc/configuration. org.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a project’s settings are a sift. yaml, or a sift. scm the project has trusted, read in four layers and validated against one schema: a key that sift does not have is refused with its position rather than ignored, and sift config show --verbose reports which layer won. doc/configuration. org has the whole of it – the discovery rules, the file-filter, the trust model, and the settings the language server reads out of the same files.

Sebagaimana diketahui, every part of the project is tested with the framework its own users already have – veritas for the library, ert for the emacs package, vim and node for the editor integrations – and none of the suite is a smoke test. org is the page: the maak tasks, what the benchmarks measure, and what the suite actually asserts. doc/development. Those tasks are also the pipeline: a pull request against trunk runs every gate before the branch lands, and only the push that lands it publishes the browser build (the pipeline).

Sebagaimana diketahui, src/sift/ is one module per job, and the dependencies run one way: records is a vocabulary, reader and format use it, the checkers use records and check/base, lint assembles them, render prints their findings, lsp delivers the same findings over a protocol, and cli wires the lot to the command line. Nothing in format or in a checker knows about ports or exit codes. The module map, and what each module owns, is doc/development. org.

Berdasarkan laporan, six premises the code is measured against: a source file is a datum, not a string; a guarantee that is not a test expires quietly; the author decides what the code says and the tool decides where the whitespace goes; a dialect is a language, not a variant; state what can be decided and report no finding otherwise; and everything a program says should be available as data. doc/design. org states them, and then the decisions that follow from them – a reader of its own, one walk with the answers kept, fuzzy formatting rather than pretty-printing, and a YAML reader small enough to audit.

Berdasarkan laporan, sift itself does not expand macros, does not type-check, and does not know a project’s conventions. That is not modesty – a linter that decided would be useless on the first project it had never seen. Where the answer can be wrong, the rule says so: wrap-in-let is a suggestion, keyword-arguments counts, and the thresholds are settings. It reports; the author decides. The language server can ask the project’s own compiler for the checking sift does not do – on open and on save, in a thread, on a temporary copy of the buffer – and publishes what that compiler says about the names, the arity and the types it can see; compiler-diagnostics: false turns the second opinion off. The language server answers the requests listed on the language server page, and answers the others with “method not found” rather than a guess.

The list of Lisp dialects that deserve a better reader is long, and each item on it is a contribution that can be carried to the end:.

The project’s own style is the style it enforces, so it formats itself:.

Docstrings are Texinfo-flavoured (@var{}, @code{}), the first line is a sentence, and each paragraph states the reason as well as the rule – which is why this README can be read without a specification beside it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a commit message is a type and then a sentence: feat: for something that did not exist before, fix: for something that was wrong, and docs:, test:, refactor:, build:, ci: or chore: for the rest, scoped in parentheses when that narrows the subject (fix(lsp):, refactor(reader):). The reader who matters is the one scanning git log for the change that broke a build, and the type is what lets nine commits in ten be skipped unopened.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, patches arrive as a pull request on github or as a patch sent with git format-patch and git send-email, which is how the author usually works. The review concerns the code.

Sebagaimana diketahui, questions are equally welcome as issues. A question that the README does not answer is a defect in the README, and reporting it is the most useful bug report there is.

Berdasarkan laporan, sift is free software under the mit license; license carries the text. A short permissive license is a practical requirement rather than a sentiment: a formatter that spreads through other people’s pipelines cannot carry a licensing question with it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, google and samsung's next face computers have arrived. Nearly two years after the companies first announced the Android XR platform that powers the hardware, the smart glasses are finally on sale.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the “intelligent eyewear” is a collaboration between the two tech companies, with samsung providing its hardware expertise and google handling much of the software platform. Smart glasses are just one part of Android XR—there are also mixed-reality headsets and glasses for more immersive experiences, like last year's Samsung Galaxy XR and the upcoming Xreal Aura.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eyewear brands warby parker and gentle monster are heavily involved in the new smart glasses, responsible for the design and fit, similar to how meta tapped ray-ban for its competing—and market-leading—wearables. (Kering Eyewear, which owns brands like Lindberg and Maui Jim, has also signed up to make glasses for Android XR in the future. Google and Samsung are leveraging Warby Parker and Gentle Monster's brick-and-mortar presence and retail expertise, which lets people demo the glasses before buying them. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, the first models are available for preorder now, with official sales starting on december 10. Warby Parker's frames start at $395 and come in three styles—Alden, Reid, and Wren—as optical or sunglasses, with various prescription, lens, and width options. Gentle Monster's glasses start at $449 and come in six designs, various colors, and tints, with prescription options for most frames.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the hardware is identical across both brands. There’s a button to capture photos and 90-second videos at up to 3K resolution with a press. Diungkapkan bahwa they are the first devices to support the “hey gemini” hotword, though you can use the well-known “hey google” hotword if you'd like. Diungkapkan bahwa “we felt that these are a gemini-forward device,” payne tells wired. You're not talking to Google, you're talking to Gemini. “It's really you and Gemini going through your day together, so it was feeling a little dissonant for us. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa oddly, these glasses are only compatible with certain devices—google pixel phones, samsung galaxy phones, and iphones—and only select models. 0 or higher, and the iPhone 13 Pro or newer. You'll need a Pixel 7 or newer, Galaxy S or Z Fold running Samsung's One UI 9. A Google spokesperson tells WIRED the company will share more about how it plans to expand support to other phones in 2027 after launch.

The arms of the glasses are similarly thick.

Diungkapkan bahwa since you'll be buying the glasses from an eyewear brand, they will be the customer-facing party to handle any problems you may have with the device or prescriptions. On the backend, Payne says there are elaborate business integrations and handoffs, so the customer service workload is split between all the companies.

Berdasarkan laporan, google has already previewed intelligent eyewear glasses with displays built into the lenses—useful for showing navigation instructions or real-time captions for folks with hearing issues. However, they are not ready yet; Payne says they're currently being tested by “non-Googlers” and are still on the road map, though he didn't share a specific release window. As for plans to launch audio-only smart glasses, like Meta's recent Ray-Ban Audio, Warby Parker co-CEO Dave Gilboa tells WIRED, “There's a pretty robust pipeline of additional products. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa smart glasses have been around for a few years, but they come in many forms. Unlike display smart glasses designed to plug into a laptop to mirror or extend your screen, or more immersive glasses like Meta's VR Glasses, which layer virtual experiences over the real world, Intelligent Eyewear is more akin to what Google pitched years ago with the original Google Glass.

Diungkapkan bahwa you can hear notifications pipe through from your connected smartphone and respond to messages by speaking to gemini. You can listen to music, take phone calls, and get audio navigation through Google Maps. Yes, you can snap photos and videos too, though Payne quickly notes that these glasses are designed more to have Gemini assist you throughout the day than to capture content.

That's likely because Meta has faced public scrutiny over how people use its smart glasses, so much so that it has spawned a new term for people wearing them: the Meta Creep (harkening back to when anyone wearing Google Glasses was called a “Glasshole”).

“We learned through Glass that you can make people uncomfortable if you're not clearly communicating,” Payne says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to that end, google is announcing a series of policies and features alongside the glasses to assuage concerns. When you ask Gemini to look at something, those visuals are not saved in your Gemini History, and Google says it will not use them to train AI models or target ads. If you try to block the indicator light while recording, the camera will stop. The glasses will automatically redact the faces of people around you before Gemini processes the visual data. They include tamper detection, so the camera will know if you tried to disable the indicator light. We've highlighted all of Google's privacy-focused announcements around its glasses in a separate story.

Gentle Monster's Intelligent Eyewear comes in six different styles.

Berdasarkan laporan, most of the features that google is positioning around intelligent eyewear rely on gemini. For example, Gemini can play music on Apple Music if you're on an iPhone. Some of these are saved in the Gemini app, but it can leverage other apps on your smartphone. See a poster for a comedy show? Just ask Gemini for more information, or add it to your calendar. You can ask Gemini to add items to your shopping list or whip up a travel itinerary with hotel recommendations and save them to a note. And if you use Samsung Notes on a Samsung phone, it'll know that's where you likely want your notes saved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you activate gemini, it's technically a “gemini live” experience, meaning the assistant activates and you can have a free-flowing conversation. A swipe back on the glasses' arm will end the interaction. When you want it to “look” at something in front of you, be specific in your query; otherwise, it won't use the camera. You can ask it to look at a page in a book and summarize the content, or if you have a bunch of cocktail ingredients in front of you but don't know what to make, you can ask Gemini for suggestions and step-by-step instructions to craft a drink—at your pace.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some gemini controls are on-device and don't need to travel to the cloud, like asking the assistant to play the next track. Speaking of, early next year, Google says users can use gestures on devices like the Fitbit Air or Google Pixel Watch to control music playback or activate Gemini on the glasses right from their wrist.

Diungkapkan bahwa another big capability is translation. Gemini will automatically detect languages and translate them to your preferred tongue. You do need to stare at the individual to hear their words translated, and there's a limited range; the quality depends heavily on the environment and noise level, but it worked remarkably well in my controlled demos, with only a few errors. The translation tries to mimic the speaker's tone and voice so it feels like their own words.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's an accessibility feature called guided vision, which provides audio descriptions for people with impaired vision, like when reading fine print or locating everyday items. Google is also collaborating with Aira so you can stream the glasses' feed straight to a human interpreter for real-time visual support.

Berdasarkan laporan, to help demystify these features—and convince consumers that smart glasses aren't just a fad for tech bros—warby parker and gentle monster are both launching pop-up experiences in new york city this week. Gentle Monster's pop-up will run for about a month, but Warby Parker's “Literatureland” will be open through 2027, letting people walk through the experience with a pair of nonprescription glasses to demo Gemini's capabilities.

Diungkapkan bahwa “these are the original wearables that have been around for hundreds of years,” warby parker's gilboa says. “A lot of people start by getting an eye exam in one of our stores, and then come in, do a demo, buy these—we just want to make it as easy and seamless as possible. ”.

#432. High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

📅 10 Nov 2026

High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/is-added-protein-in-packaged-food-really-healthier?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. It also helps to make meals feel filling. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. Great! But.

Diungkapkan bahwa once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. (I've done the math for various body weights here. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. ) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i've been performing maximum reps every hour while seated during my workday, and i've noticed a few things so far. Read on to find out more.

A soleus push-up (SPU) is a seated calf raise exercise that targets the deeper calf, or soleus muscles.

Berdasarkan laporan, collectively, the soleus and gastrocnemius muscles form your calves and are referred to as a secondary heart. These muscles help pump blood toward the heart, squeezing the veins with contractions so oxygen-depleted blood travels up the body rather than pooling in your lower limbs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to keep circulation going, being as active as possible helps, including walking, running, or cycling. You may also find elevating your legs at times can be useful, especially after prolonged sitting. But if you don't fancy swinging your legs up onto your desk in the office, seated calf raises or soleus push-ups can help.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but before we get into what happened when i tried it every hour, every day, for one week during work, there's a study i think you should know about. Published in the Journal of Biomechanics, the research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the deeper soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts. ".

Performing these muscular contractions seated can be useful for people who have desk jobs or want to limit fatigue and blood pressure issues.

Here's what happened when I tried the exercise every day.

Diungkapkan bahwa research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the powerful soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts. ".

I have very mobile, clicky joints, and my ankles get both noisy and stiff if I don't move often enough, so adding as many reps as I could for 60 seconds per hour during my workday really helped.

I set eight alarms, one for every hour, and timed myself for 60 seconds, performing reps at my desk while still working.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when i got up to move around, particularly later in the week, i found my ankles felt more mobile and warmed up, and my calves felt less stiff. I recommend learning how to do calf raises, as well as trying some ankle mobility exercises and lower-body stretches alongside this move to ramp things up further.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, because the movement is driven from the lower limbs while seated, it's extremely accessible and low-impact, meaning most people don't even need to stop working while performing the soleus push-up. That also means you can go for high rep ranges while sitting at a desk.

The soleus muscles thrive on sustained periods of movement, so this makes it an ideal exercise to repeat during the week while keeping those muscle contractions going during seated periods.

Diungkapkan bahwa i added ankle weights to increase the intensity, and this is safe to do because there's no impact. I found it worked my muscles harder and, after stopping 60 seconds later, I felt like I'd been walking up a set of stairs. Add weights just above your knees for even more resistance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, marc hamilton pioneered the soleus push-up at the university of houston and published findings in the journal iscience, saying the exercise provides "optimal activation" and "elevates muscle metabolism for hours, even while sitting. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he adds that the exercise helps sustain an "elevated local oxidative metabolism" which can improve blood glucose regulation by helping clear blood glucose from the bloodstream. Oxidative metabolism refers to a process where oxygen helps burn blood glucose or fats, depending on the energy needs of your working muscles.

Diungkapkan bahwa “no one ever investigated how to use it to optimize our health, until now,” says hamilton. “When activated correctly, the soleus muscle can raise local oxidative metabolism to high levels for hours, not just minutes, and does so by using a different fuel mixture. ”.

Of course, without a carefully controlled lab setting, I couldn't tell you if this made a difference for me or not.

I can be subject to swollen ankles and a little numbness in certain positions, a condition my musculoskeletal doctor hasn't been able to pinpoint just yet, so I was intrigued that soleus push-ups could boost circulation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a week later, although not life-changing, i have noticed less swelling and numbness while sitting. This makes sense, as your soleus muscle helps pump blood toward the heart.

Berdasarkan laporan, plus, as we age, calf strength can decline, which can have a knock-on impact on gait and balance during movement. By maintaining strong, healthy calves, I know I'm reducing the workload on my joints, namely my ankles and knees, which should benefit me heading into my later years.

Keeping them strong can make everyday activities feel easier, too, while also improving balance, ankle stability and overall lower-limb function.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, according to science, these muscles protect your heart, aid circulation, help produce movement, and impact gait and balance. What more reason do you need to give this exercise a try the next time you're seated?.

#436. Talking Zen 6 with Mike Clark at AMD In-Depth

📅 11 Nov 2026

Talking Zen 6 with Mike Clark at AMD In-Depth

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://chipsandcheese.com/p/talking-zen-6-with-mike-clark-at

Hello you fine Internet folks,I sat down with AMD’s Mike Clark to talk about Zen 6, the evolution from Zen 5 and what some of the differences are between Zen 6 and Zen 6c and what drove some of those changes.

The transcript below has been edited for readability and conciseness.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: hello, you fine internet folks. We’re here at AMD In-Depth, where we’re talking about Venice. With me, I have a returning guest, Mike Clark. Would you like to tell the audience who you are?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: hi, i’m mike clark, the original architect of zen. Some people refer to me as “Zen Daddy. ” I’ve been working on cores here at AMD for 33 years, and we’ve got another great one coming, so I’m very proud of the design team I get to represent here today.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: i’ve had some hands-on time with zen 6c. Let’s talk about the change that’s happened with Zen 6 and Zen 6c, what I refer to in my piece as the Zen 6 family. Why is it different from previous generations?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: right. Before, we were really just using the denser technology as an area play. And our dense technology is now our top-of-the-line, no-questions-asked performance core, because we’ve also enabled the full L3 in that implementation, at 4MB per core. So if you look more in-depth at what we have, what used to be our classic design, we now think of as our high-frequency design. Starting with Zen 4, we’ve been going through this evolution of having two core families. In this generation, having learned a lot, as we were filling out that denser version of the core, we wanted to leverage it to add some extra IPC within the core. So we have 32 of those cores, 128MB of L3, and the highest IPC you can get in that core.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: awesome. So far, one thing I’ve noticed is that the vector scheduler is a bit bigger on Zen 6c. What was the reasoning for increasing that on Zen 6c?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: well, that wasn’t the only thing we increased. But because of its reduced frequency target, Zen 6c can have a little more capacity in the queues, since it doesn’t have to reach the maximum frequency the high-frequency core has to hit. We want them to have the same fit and feel, so the same optimizations apply to both. One principle we follow is that we don’t want to create a delta between the two architectures that software has to be optimized for. The floating-point scheduler is just one example. There are other queues throughout the core that are larger in Zen 6c, to pull out a little more IPC and get a little more leverage in that SMT environment as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: interesting. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c build on the design you had in Zen 5, and one of the interesting things with Zen 5 was the dual decode setup. Has the front end changed much to let a single thread make better use of both decode clusters?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mike clark: yes. But it gets quite complicated with one thread running larger-footprint workloads, where some of it might be hitting the I-cache and some of it might be hitting the op cache, and you’re trying to get everything synced up. As you said, Zen 5 was a new foundation, with the ability to fetch two basic blocks and get them down the line. So we spent a lot of time optimizing that and making it more efficient from both a delivery and a power perspective: less power wasted, and more efficient delivery from that new front end.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: awesome. Going down into the execution engine, I also noticed that the number of integer multiply units has gone down from three to two. Could you talk a bit about what drove that choice?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: it really came out of the zen 5 design, where we had a more unified scheduler. To make a scheduler simpler, you want the units it schedules into to be very uniform, and the way we had set up those schedulers, adding a third multiplier to the group it was scheduling into was easy and didn’t add complication. In Zen 6, we realized that to really scale out the architecture, we needed to go back to more distributed schedulers, which now schedule into the ALUs. We hadn’t seen much uptick from that extra multiplier on Zen 5, so to optimize the area and the schedulers, we went back to two multipliers.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: speaking of integer multiply, on the vector side you’ve added two more vnni units. What was the impetus for adding them, and at what point in the design did you add them?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: as i said in the talk, these are long design programs. So we were always focused on making the core good at AI. It’s not going to beat a GPU, and that’s not the point. But Zen 5 was a whole new foundation for AI workloads, and we’ve always believed the core has a place in AI: orchestration, data type manipulation, smaller models. When we started, no one was really even using that term. We weren’t designing Zen 6 to be an agentic core. We realized we probably should have some more VNNI, given where we were seeing inference go, and the team rallied around that. It was kind of late, since these are long-lead projects and the floor plan was set, but the team rallied, we were able to squeeze a couple more VNNI pipes in there, and it was a big success.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: again on the vector side, one of the oddities of zen 5 was that although the wires were all there, the load unit could only do two vector loads at a time. What changed within the Zen 6 core to allow four vector loads, assuming they’re either 128 or 256 bits?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: we can do the 256-bit loads. Since we were able to do two 512-bit loads, we already had 1,024 wires headed over there. Obviously, using them piecemeal versus as one contiguous set complicates the design. I think it’s something we always wanted to do on Zen 5, but with all the change and getting it working, we left that for the Zen 6 team, and they were awesome. We’re all really one team at AMD anyway, and sometimes things intersect at different points in the roadmap. This was the time to do it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: speaking of bandwidth into the caches, the l2 in zen 5 had some oddities where it couldn’t always hit 64 bytes per cycle on reads. What changed in Zen 6 to allow that? Because I’ve been able to measure it, and it does hit that.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: honestly, sometimes you just don’t see some of these things. A lot of it was that we would be over-prefetching, and prefetches that hit in the L2 would be robbing L2 bandwidth. So we made sure we could sustain those prefetches alongside demand requests, reduce the conflicts, and deliver the full 64 bytes per cycle that we want.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: awesome. What I also noticed, which is really neat, is that there wasn’t any reduction in accuracy. There seems to have been a reduction in branch misprediction latency, so when you miss a branch, the number of cycles it takes to recover has gone down. Circling all the way back to the front: the all-important branch predictor. So how did you pull off not only a faster branch predictor, but one that’s even slightly more accurate than Zen 5’s already very accurate predictor?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mike clark: the branch prediction team, as you know, is very algorithmic. And we’re always focused on our pipeline length. So each generation, we’re monomaniacally focused on getting going again as fast as we can when we’re wrong. It’s a great optimization problem: the number of TAGE tables, how much information they hold, accuracy. There’s lots of design space and lots of exploration, and AI has even been getting involved in helping us figure out how to optimize it. That was an area where we didn’t really want to grow; we thought we could be more efficient in the way we lay out the tables for prediction. There are lots of unique tricks we pull to get that redirect back into the front end and get it flowing as fast as possible. So we set out to make a more efficient one. No matter how good a branch predictor you build, there are always hard-to-predict branches, and you’re always going to mispredict. And you’ve observed it, which is great.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: yeah. Wrapping this all up and moving outside the core into the L3, there are obviously topology differences between the 12-core and 32-core CCDs. That’s very impressive, especially considering the clock deficit. I haven’t had time on Zen 6 yet, but I have had time on Zen 6c, and in SPECint 2026 it matches your fastest Zen 5 server CPU. How much were you able to mitigate those differences inside the core, building up structures to tolerate latency, to compensate for the slightly increased L3 latency?.

Berdasarkan laporan, mike clark: as i always talk about, the design has to be balanced. As we grow the capacity of a structure, the new technology helps it shrink, so the physical distance doesn’t grow linearly, but unfortunately the distance does grow. Inside the L3, there are a lot of tricks I can’t talk about.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: [in order to] maintain bandwidth within the l3 mesh so we can keep delivering to the cores. And in the cores, we do grow the queues to handle those higher latencies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: awesome. My penultimate question: Verano is adding LPDDR5X to the EPYC ecosystem. Were there any design considerations between LPDDR5X and DDR5 that you had to think about when designing the core?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: at the ccx level, we focus a lot on bandwidth per core. I think Mahesh talked a lot about the SDP ports, with 32-byte reads per port, so we try to make sure we have enough bandwidth between the CCD and the IOD. But we were already well provisioned for bandwidth with MRDIMMs, so that construction, the winglets and choosing a different memory technology, didn’t really have a major impact on how we built the core.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: awesome. Usually this is where I’d ask what your favorite type of cheese is, but since we already know that: have you tried any new cheeses lately?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: i have. My new favorite is Cotija cheese.

Mike Clark: I’ve been eating a lot of tacos.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: thanks for having me, george. I always look forward to coming and talking with you about what this awesome AMD CPU design team has created, and you always have so many good questions. I wish I could answer more, since we do have to protect our secret sauce, but I really enjoy helping you understand some of our thought processes, the challenges we face, and how we’ve been able to overcome them.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: well, it’s always fun to sit down with you and talk, not just about what you’re doing, but also what the team is doing and what you’re looking forward to in the future. So thank you so much.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: i’ll see you in the next one. Have a good one, folks!.

#437. This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/this-actively-exploited-security-vulnerability-is-putting-your-chrome-browser?utm_medium=RSS

Berdasarkan laporan, if you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws to exploit them, while researchers want to block hackers from doing so. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday update included more than 1,400 patches; meanwhile, Apple's latest security update fixed two iMessage flaws that let both bad actors and innocent parties alike access texts they shouldn't.

Diungkapkan bahwa whether you use a mac or a pc, you probably browse the web with chrome, or a chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as reported by the hacker news, google released a new update for chrome on monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Berdasarkan laporan, use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that's bad enough on the surface, but, unfortunately, google confirmed that cve-2026-125350 has an active exploit in the wild. The company is keeping other details close to the vest, but it's dangerous nonetheless. At least someone, somewhere, has used this flaw against a target, which puts all Chrome users (as well as users of Chromium-based browsers) at risk.

Berdasarkan laporan, what's more, this isn't chrome's first active exploit of the year—this is its eighth. The company is playing catch-up with hackers looking to target users of its browser, which makes sense, seeing as Chrome is by far the world's most popular browser.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you're using chrome on your computer, you'll want to update it as soon as possible. 0. 50 on Linux. 8103. 0. 51 on Mac or PC, or 157. 50/. 8103. Make sure you're running at least versions 157. To check, click the three dots in the top-right corner of your Chrome window, then go to More > Help > About Google Chrome.

Berdasarkan laporan, other chromium-based browsers may not have the update yet, but they are affected by this flaw. If you use browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Brave, keep an eye on your updates to install any of the latest patches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, without the redesigned health app, none of the new features appeal to me all that much. But performance improvements, bug fixes, and security fixes are always welcomed. What most of really wants is faster and more reliable Siri AI, along with support for a wider range of personal data, such as PDF documents on the iCloud Drive.

New Episodes contains only the latest episodes from shows you follow, while Continue Playing is a hub for all the episodes you’ve previously started but haven’t yet finished.

Diungkapkan bahwa apple’s games app introduces some small updates in ios 27. 2 as well.

Berdasarkan laporan, the home tab now shows you recently downloaded games that you haven’t yet played. And Apple says achievement progress and leaderboard scores have been updated in the Home tab to be easier to track. Previously, you would only see games with some play activity. Finally, the Friends tab “provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages” per Apple.
